title: Finite orbits and invariant refinements of clopen partitions
statement: Use the small universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $G$ be a compact Hausdorff topological group such that every neighbourhood of $1$ contains an open normal subgroup. Let $P$ be a compact topological space with a continuous left action $G\times P\to P$. A finite clopen partition of $P$ is a finite set of pairwise disjoint nonempty open and closed subsets whose union is $P$; for $P=\varnothing$ the empty partition is allowed. For every such partition $\alpha$, there is an open normal subgroup $N\subseteq G$ such that $nA=A$ for all $n\in N$ and $A\in\alpha$. The orbit $\mathcal T=\{g\alpha:g\in G\}$, where $g\alpha=\{gA:A\in\alpha\}$, is finite. The collection $\beta$ of nonempty intersections obtained by choosing one block from each member of $\mathcal T$ is a finite clopen partition refining $\alpha$, and $G$ permutes its blocks.

proof.text: If $P=\varnothing$, take $N=G$: the only partition and every translate are empty, so $\mathcal T=\{\varnothing\}$ and there are no choices of a block from its member; thus $\beta=\varnothing$. Henceforth let $P\ne\varnothing$. Each $A\in\alpha$ is compact by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-in-quasi-compact], since it is closed in compact $P$.

source.place: Tag 005C, label lemma-closed-in-quasi-compact; empty-space clause checked directly.

proof.text: Write $a:G\times P\to P$ for the action. For each $A\in\alpha$, $a^{-1}(A)$ is open and contains $\{1\}\times A$. The singleton $\{1\}$ is compact (one member of any open cover covers it). Apply [lem-sfb-compact-product-open-neighborhoods] with $K=\{1\}$, $L=A$, $W=a^{-1}(A)$: obtain an open neighborhood $U_A$ of $1$ with $U_A A\subseteq A$.

source.place: generalized_tube_lemma, lines 752–759; compact-product neighborhood input to the agent expansion of Bhatt–Scholze Example 4.1.10, p. 28.

proof.text: The finite intersection $U=\bigcap_{A\in\alpha}U_A$ is an open neighborhood of $1$. The assumed open-normal-subgroup basis gives an open normal subgroup $N\subseteq U$. For $n\in N$ we have $nA\subseteq A$ and $n^{-1}A\subseteq A$; applying $n$ to the latter inclusion gives $A\subseteq nA$. Therefore $nA=A$ for every block.

source.place: Example 4.1.10, p. 28: agent expansion of the pro-finite-discrete-G-set presentation; finite invariant clopen quotient construction.

proof.text: Each left coset $gN$ is open: left multiplication by $g$ has continuous inverse left multiplication by $g^{-1}$. These cosets cover compact $G$, so finitely many $g_1N,\ldots,g_rN$ cover $G$. If $g=g_i n$ with $n\in N$, then $g\alpha=g_i(n\alpha)=g_i\alpha$. Consequently $\mathcal T\subseteq\{g_1\alpha,\ldots,g_r\alpha\}$ is finite.

source.place: Example 4.1.10, p. 28: agent expansion of the pro-finite-discrete-G-set presentation; finite invariant clopen quotient construction.

proof.text: For fixed $g$, the maps $p\mapsto gp$ and $p\mapsto g^{-1}p$ are continuous inverse maps. Thus $g\alpha$ is a finite clopen partition. There are finitely many choices of one block $A_\gamma$ from each $\gamma\in\mathcal T$. Their intersections are clopen; discard the empty ones to obtain $\beta$. Each $p\in P$ selects its unique block in every $\gamma$, so lies in one such intersection. Two distinct choices differ at some $\gamma$ and give disjoint intersections. Since $\alpha=1\alpha\in\mathcal T$, every block of $\beta$ lies in a block of $\alpha$.

source.place: Example 4.1.10, p. 28: agent expansion of the pro-finite-discrete-G-set presentation; finite invariant clopen quotient construction.

proof.text: For $h\in G$, $\gamma\mapsto h\gamma$ bijects $\mathcal T$ with itself, with inverse multiplication by $h^{-1}$. The bijection $p\mapsto hp$ gives $h(\bigcap_\gamma A_\gamma)=\bigcap_\gamma hA_\gamma$; reindexing by $h\gamma$ exhibits this as another defining intersection for $\beta$. It is nonempty whenever the original is. Applying $h^{-1}$ proves that $h$ bijects the blocks of $\beta$, as required.
